draft.title: Balanced chemical equations
card: A chemical equation shows reactants on the left and products on the right, with an arrow between them. Each formula has a number in front, called a coefficient, that says how many of that substance react or form.
A balanced equation has the same number of each kind of atom on both sides. Atoms are only rearranged, so none can appear or vanish.

To balance an equation, change the coefficients only. Never change the small numbers inside a formula, because that would make a different substance. For example, 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O has 4 H atoms and 2 O atoms on each side.
State symbols follow each formula: (s) solid, (l) liquid, (g) gas and (aq) dissolved in water. Example: 2H₂(g) + O₂(g) → 2H₂O(l).
draft.remember: Balance by changing coefficients only, so each atom count matches. State symbols show the form of each substance.

a.q: Magnesium burns in oxygen. Which of these equations shows the reaction with the same atoms on both sides?
opts: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO
Mg + O₂ → MgO
Mg + O₂ → 2MgO
2Mg + 2O₂ → 2MgO
a.why: 2Mg + O₂ → 2MgO has 2 Mg and 2 O on each side. Mg + O₂ → MgO looks tempting because each formula is correct, but it has 2 O atoms on the left and only 1 on the right.
a.clue: Count the Mg atoms and the O atoms on each side.

b.q: A student balances H₂ + O₂ → H₂O by changing the product to H₂O₂. Why is this wrong, and what is the right fix?
opts: It changes the substance; put a 2 in front of H₂O
It changes the substance; put a 2 in front of O₂
It is fine, because both sides now have 2 O atoms
It is fine, because the state symbols are still missing
b.why: Changing a small number inside a formula makes a different substance, since H₂O₂ is not water. Only coefficients can change, so write 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O. The option saying it is fine is tempting because the atom counts match, but the product is no longer water.
b.clue: Which numbers are you allowed to change?

b.best: It changes the substance; put a 2 in front of H₂O

problems.detail: The intended option says the right fix is to put a 2 in front of H₂O. That alone gives H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O, with 2 H atoms on the left and 4 on the right, which is still unbalanced. The full fix, 2H₂ + O₂ → 2H₂O as the why says, also needs a 2 in front of H₂. The option should name both coefficients.

The card says each formula has a number in front, called a coefficient. But in its own examples O₂ has no number shown. It should say that a coefficient of 1 is not written, or younger students may be confused.

check.summary: In question b, the keyed fix (a 2 in front of H₂O only) still leaves the equation unbalanced; it also needs a 2 in front of H₂. The card should also say that a coefficient of 1 is not written.
